_readme: Canonical machine-readable Anthropic list prices. Consume this file; do not transcribe its numbers into code. Human narrative, role guidance and API-shape notes live in ../ANTHROPIC_MODEL_REFERENCE.md, which is canonical for everything except the numbers below — those are canonical HERE, and the markdown table is generated-equivalent. Fix a price in this file first, then reconcile the markdown.

provenance.staleness_rule: If today is more than staleness_days after verified_on, treat every rate here as suspect: say so when advising, and re-verify against source before quoting a cost. Check this by date comparison at read time — never call the Models API on the advice path (it cannot supply pricing anyway).

units.note: input and output are list rates. Cache and batch rates are NOT listed per model — they are fixed multipliers on the input rate (see multipliers). Deriving them prevents the half-landed correction where a base rate is fixed and its hand-copied cache column is not.

multipliers.note: cache_write_5m applies to bare `cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'}`. Adding `ttl: '1h'` moves the write to cache_write_1h — a 60% increase that is invisible unless the consumer models both. batch applies to BOTH directions on the Message Batches API and is routinely forgotten on asynchronous bulk jobs.

claude-mythos-5.availability: Project Glasswing participants only; capability and pricing twin of Fable 5

fast.note: speed: 'fast' (beta fast-mode-2026-02-01), Claude API only. Pricing a fast-mode call at the standard rate understates it by 2x.

claude-sonnet-5.note: $2/$10 is PERMANENT. It launched as introductory pricing 'through 2026-08-31' and the scheduled rise to $3/$15 was cancelled. Any table or comment still asserting the reversion is wrong and over-budgets Sonnet 5 by 50%. Sonnet 4.6 is therefore both older and 50% dearer — never pick it for new work.

claude-sonnet-4-6.note: Dearer than Sonnet 5 and a generation older. Priced here only so a consumer costing historical telemetry gets it right.

unknown_model_policy.rule: Do not silently invent a price for an unlisted model id. Either raise, or fall back to the MOST expensive rate in the model's family so the estimate over-reports rather than under-reports — and say which you did. A spend guard that quietly guesses a rate is not a guard.

caveats.tokeniser: Models from Opus 4.7 onward emit ~30% more tokens for the same text than 4.6-and-earlier, so comparing headline $/token across that boundary overstates the saving. Measured (small-model-lab, 2026-08-14) on 40 identical requests: Sonnet 4.6 $0.39 vs Sonnet 5 $0.49 at then-identical prices, +26%. Sonnet 5's effective rate against a 4.6-era baseline is ~$2.52/$12.60 — still cheaper than Sonnet 4.6, by ~16% rather than the headline 33%.
caveats.list_vs_billed: These are list rates: no Batch API discount, no account-specific or negotiated discount. An estimate built from them is comparable across projects and telemetry, but it is not an invoice.
caveats.effort: On output-heavy jobs `output_config.effort` moves spend further than model choice. Measured on structured extraction: Sonnet 5 at effort low cost 37% less than medium and agreed 0.985, while Opus 5 at 2.5x the price agreed only 0.962. Probe effort before assuming a bigger model is the upgrade.

consumers._note: Projects that hold a copy of these rates, and the check that keeps each honest. Keep this current — it is what makes a price correction traceable to everything it affects. Every entry's copy is also audited byte-for-byte by ai-knowledge/scripts/knowhub-doctor.sh (protocol channel).

aigent-alpha.note: Also holds src/aigent_alpha/em/charter.py EM_MODEL_PRICES, deliberately FROZEN for the EM-Q3 epoch by docs/specs/2026-08-10-em-q3-lane-a-charter.md. It pins Sonnet 5 at $3/$15 (50% above canonical). Changing it is a charter amendment, not a drift fix; the check reports the divergence as a WARN.
